prompt.context: Our client, Kid Country, is the purveyor of an increasingly unpopular form of hybrid rap/rock/country music. An early boom in the market for awful music allowed him to amass a substantial war chest and offer products (music related) in a variety of areas. His accountants have recently informed him of consistently declining revenues over the last three years and encouraged him to seek outside expertise.
prompt.question: Kid Country has been experiencing declining revenues over the last three years. He has asked us to diagnose the problem and recommend how to improve the business.

clarifying_info.q: What lines of business does Kid Country operate?
clarifying_info.a: Apparel (tasteless t-shirts), beverages (tasteless beer), CD/MP3 sales, and concert ticket sales.

clarifying_info.q: Are revenue trends the same across all lines of business?
clarifying_info.a: Overall revenue numbers are down, but trends vary across lines of business. Specifics will be addressed as we dig in.
Profitability trends also vary by line of business. We will get into those as well.

exhibits.title: 2014 Sales by Line of Business
exhibits.shows: Stacked bar chart showing 2014 forecasted sales ($M) broken into three cost/profit segments for four product lines: Apparel, CD/MP3, Concert Tickets, and Beverages.

exhibits.title: 2011 Sales by Line of Business
exhibits.shows: Stacked bar chart showing 2011 sales ($M) broken into three cost/profit segments for three product lines: Apparel, CD/MP3, and Concert Tickets. Beverages does not appear, indicating it was not a line of business in 2011.

exhibits.title: Tour Forecast Data
exhibits.shows: Table showing tour forecast data for the proposed new deal, with columns for Tour Dates, Ticket Price, Tickets/Show, Beer Price, Beers/Show, % of Own Brand Beers, Ticket Margin, and Beer Margin. The promoters propose dramatically lower ticket prices, increased venue cut, back-to-back shows, and exclusive sale of Kid Country's own 'Real American Red White and Blue Lager' at venues.
exhibits.data: Detailed numerical forecasts are provided in the exhibit; the interviewer guidance page (exhibit_p227.png) contains the answer key for these figures.

framework: Identify which lines of business are driving revenue decline vs. holding steady
Analyze the basic economic levers within each line of business (revenue, costs, profitability)
Consider both internal factors (product quality, brand) and external factors (channels, competition, trends) affecting each lever
Prioritize lines of business by opportunity: shore up core, grow promising segments, fix or exit weak ones

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibits 1 and 2, how is each line of business performing? What are the key takeaways?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates should identify: (1) Concert Tickets = core business with highest revenue, highest absolute profit, and best profitability, but declining due to unfashionable music. (2) Apparel = weak performer with very low profitability ($0.25M profit on ~$5.25M sales) and little improvement since 2011. (3) CD/MP3 = high sales but declining, low profitability squeezed by channel margins (Spotify, Pandora, iTunes); Kid Country lacks leverage to fight back against channels. (4) Beverages = growth opportunity with high profitability ($3M profit on ~$4.5M sales), but newly added since 2011 (does not appear in Exhibit 2).

questions.prompt: What initial recommendations would you make based on the exhibit analysis, before the promoter proposal is introduced?
questions.guidance: Shore up the core ticket business (it drives the brand and all side businesses). Capitalize on the high-margin beverages opportunity. Kill or fix the apparel line (very low profitability). Address the channel margin squeeze on CD/MP3 by noting Kid Country lacks leverage, so this line may be managed down or abandoned.

questions.prompt: Kid Country has received a proposal from his concert promoters that would substantially change the business model of his tours. The promoters have negotiated a deal with venues: if Kid Country drops ticket prices dramatically (while increasing venues' cut), venues will allow back-to-back shows (same night or consecutive nights) and will carry exclusively Kid Country's own 'Real American Red White and Blue Lager' during shows. Using Exhibit 3, build a profit calculation and make a go/no-go recommendation.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a clean, well-organized profit calculation table using the Exhibit 3 data. Key steps: (1) Calculate ticket revenue and profit per show under new pricing. (2) Calculate beer revenue and profit per show, factoring in % of own brand beers. (3) Double the number of shows (back-to-back). (4) Assume negligible incremental costs for the second show (almost all venue costs are fixed). (5) Compare total profit under the new model versus the current model. Note: The venues' profits go from $2M to $2.4M under the deal, confirming it is good for venues too. Strong candidates will avoid unnecessary calculations and use the margins provided.

math.setup: Use Exhibit 3 columns: Ticket Price x Tickets/Show x Ticket Margin = Ticket Profit per Show. Beer Price x Beers/Show x (% Own Brand) x Beer Margin = Own Beer Profit per Show. Multiply by 2 shows (back-to-back) for total. Compare to current single-show profit.
steps: Ticket profit per show = Ticket Price x Tickets/Show x Ticket Margin
Beer profit per show = Beer Price x Beers/Show x % Own Brand x Beer Margin
Total profit per date = 2 x (Ticket Profit + Beer Profit) [negligible extra costs for second show]
Compare new total profit to current baseline (using 2014 trends implying declining performance)
math.answer: Go/No-Go depends on calculated profit improvement; strong candidates will show the math table clearly and note the directional improvement from beer margins offsetting lower ticket margins, with doubled show volume driving overall profitability up.

recommendation: Accept the promoter proposal if the profit calculation shows a net improvement — beverage margins and doubled show volume likely more than offset lower ticket prices
Prioritize the beverages line of business as the highest-margin growth opportunity
Consider restructuring or exiting the apparel line given persistently low profitability
Manage CD/MP3 as a declining segment given channel margin pressure from Spotify, Pandora, and iTunes
risks: The proposal fundamentally redefines Kid Country's core business — he effectively becomes a brewer who uses music to sell beer; brand implications must be considered
Doubling the number of shows is a massive personal burden on Kid Country — he must be willing to perform twice as many shows
Beverage business scalability is unproven — can Kid Country scale his brewing/distribution to meet demand at all venues?
Declining music popularity is a structural headwind; even with the new model, ticket volumes may continue to fall
Re-branding to a different musical style is likely not feasible
next_steps: Validate beverage supply chain and production capacity to support exclusive venue deals at scale
Quantify personal and operational costs of doubling show frequency
Model downside scenarios (continued ticket volume decline) to stress-test the go/no-go decision
Explore whether the apparel line can be repositioned or sold off
Investigate whether Kid Country can negotiate better terms with digital music channels over time
